acceptance.given: A validator or test invocation is defined using the Package A public invocation contract and its caller controls process execution.

oracle.expected: The invocation is represented as a literal argv array, is executed with shell disabled, and has a finite positive timeout supplied by the caller; the invocation record or harness assertion exposes these properties.
forbidden: A shell-formatted command string is used as the machine command contract.
The invocation executes without a finite positive caller-assigned timeout.
The validator or test infers timeout or command semantics from an unparsed shell string.
oracle.observable: The validation harness or integration test inspects the invocation arguments and timeout before or during execution and records a structured pass/fail assertion for argv form, shell=False, and positive finite timeout.

acceptance.then: The machine invocation contract is an argv vector and the caller supplies a finite positive timeout, with shell execution disabled where the contract requires it.
acceptance.when: During construction and execution of the validator or terminal pytest invocation, evaluate the command representation and timeout at the harness boundary.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A planned integration or terminal test intentionally supplies a shell command string or omits, unbounds, or sets a non-positive timeout; the invocation guard fails with an assertion identifying the invalid command-contract or timeout field.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce validator invocation boundaries using literal argv vectors, shell-disabled execution, and finite positive caller-assigned timeouts.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted state or schema migration; reverting restores the prior validator entrypoint behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: Invocation definitions transition from unspecified or shell-based execution to explicit argv with caller-assigned finite timeout and shell-disabled execution.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted migration/integration selector and the Package A terminal pytest command assert literal argv, shell=False, and a finite positive timeout at the invocation boundary.
